name: Quantum Pi Benchmark (QPB)
description: The Quantum Pi Benchmark (QPB) separates oracle-construction provenance, controller blindness, demonstrated capability, execution layer, and provider access rather than compressing them into a vendor score. This paper tests whether the architecture-neutral information flow established in the Benchmark can be carried through additional provider stacks, using Microsoft Azure’s platform, and records the point at which each accessible path stops. The frozen record contains 20 accepted analysis rows mapped to 16 unique jobs: fourteen Rigetti ideal Quantum Virtual Machine (QVM) jobs and two Quantinuum H2-1E noisy-emulator jobs. It contains zero quantum processing unit (QPU) jobs. The Rigetti campaign implements an N = 4, one-iteration search and an eight-job control suite through logical Quil and Azure-hosted quilc/QVM. Six candidate circuits return the marked address in 256/256 shots; matched-search and no-hit controls remain near the 1/4 reference, two Ramsey controls return their expected event in 1,024/1,024 shots, and four basis roundtrips return 1,024/1,024. The evidence supports P3/B0 validation but no hardware rung or hardware-evidence claim. The Quantinuum campaign validates all sixteen finite Bailey–Borwein–Plouffe (BBP) arithmetic trajectories, compiles N = 16 provenance class 3 / blindness class 0 / capability-rung 5 (P3/B0/R5)-candidate circuits into an H2-native basis, audits provider Open Quantum Assembly Language (OpenQASM) transport, and executes them on H2-1E.
